expectations.text: Defines the deemed export rule: releasing ITAR technical data to a foreign person in the US is an export to their country/countries of nationality
expectations.evidence: "A 'deemed export' occurs the moment ITAR-controlled technical data... is released to a foreign national... treated as an export to that person's country of citizenship (or countries, if dual national)", even "entirely inside the United States".

expectations.text: States a license/authorization (e.g., DSP-5) is required unless an exemption applies, judged as if exporting to that nationality
expectations.evidence: "any ITAR technical data disclosure to them is a deemed export unless authorized"; "determine whether their country of citizenship requires a license/TAA"; "obtain the TAA (22 CFR § 124.1) or individual license before granting any access".

expectations.text: Covers what counts as release: visual access, oral disclosure, physical access to hardware revealing technical data, IT system access
expectations.evidence: "blueprints, drawings, specifications, source code, test reports, or oral/visual disclosure"; "even verbal walkthroughs in a design review"; "IT access controls"; "controlled physical areas".

expectations.text: Recommends a Technology Control Plan: access controls, segregated systems, badging/escort, training, screening of nationalities against §126.1
expectations.evidence: "Stand up a Technology Control Plan (TCP): physical segregation... IT access controls... visitor/escort procedures... annual ITAR training"; "§ 126.1 proscribed/embargoed countries (Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Venezuela)" screening.

expectations.text: Notes dual/third nationalities considerations and that US persons include green-card holders (foreign person = not US citizen/permanent resident/protected person)
expectations.evidence: "countries, if dual national"; "capture citizenship (all citizenships if dual)"; "A green card holder (lawful permanent resident) is a 'US person' under 22 CFR § 120.62"; "Protected persons under 8 USC § 1324b... treated as US persons".
